title: Computational Thinking & Creativity
summary: Students begin their journey by learning how computers 'think' through logic puzzles and unplugged activities. The focus is on understanding sequences and cause-and-effect before moving to screens.

terms.title: Foundations of Logic
terms.outcomes: Understanding sequences, patterns, and cause-and-effect through unplugged activities.

terms.title: Algorithms in Daily Life
terms.outcomes: Developing step-by-step instructions for everyday tasks (e.g., making a sandwich) to understand algorithmic thinking.

terms.title: Digital Logic Games
terms.outcomes: Applying logic to solve puzzles in games like Lightbot and Scratch Jr, introducing loops and conditionals visually.

terms.title: Creative Coding Project
terms.outcomes: Creating a simple interactive story or animation using block-based coding, emphasizing creativity and expression.

safety: Introduces the concept of rules in games as analogous to laws and safety guidelines online. Fair play and kindness in digital spaces are emphasized.

title: The Brain: Raspberry Pi & LEDs
summary: The core of the phone—the Raspberry Pi computer—is introduced. Students learn to set up the operating system and write their first Python scripts to control simple electronic circuits.

terms.title: Unboxing the Brain
terms.outcomes: Introduction to the Raspberry Pi. Identifying ports (USB, HDMI, GPIO) and setting up the Operating System.

terms.title: Hello World (Physical)
terms.outcomes: Building a simple circuit on a breadboard to light up an LED. Understanding voltage, current, and resistance.

terms.title: Coding the Light
terms.outcomes: Using Python to control the LED (blink, flash patterns). Bridging the gap between software code and physical hardware.

terms.title: Traffic Light Project
terms.outcomes: Simulating a traffic light sequence using multiple LEDs and Python logic. Introduction to timing and loops.

safety: Basic electrical safety (short circuits). Introduction to the concept that hardware can be controlled by software, and that malicious software could potentially misuse hardware.

title: Input: Sensors & Environment
summary: Focusing on how devices perceive the world, students work with sensors that detect touch, motion, and light. This module lays the groundwork for understanding how phones respond to user environment.

terms.title: The Sense of Touch
terms.outcomes: Implementing capacitive touch sensors. replacing physical buttons with touch interfaces.

terms.title: Motion and Orientation
terms.outcomes: Interfacing with an Accelerometer/Gyroscope. Detecting tilt and shake gestures.

terms.title: Environmental Awareness
terms.outcomes: Reading light and temperature sensors. Creating automated reactions (e.g., screen auto-brightness).

terms.title: Smart Sensor Hub
terms.outcomes: A mini-project combining multiple sensors to log environmental data or control outputs based on gestures.

safety: Privacy implication of sensors: Discussing how apps can track physical activity (steps/motion) and environment. Students learn what data can be inferred from simple sensor readings.

title: Connectivity: Wi-Fi & Bluetooth
summary: The device connects to the world as students explore the invisible networks that link computers. Practical exercises involve scanning for networks and sending messages between devices.

terms.title: Wireless Basics
terms.outcomes: Understanding radio waves. Scanning for Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth devices using the Pi.

terms.title: Client and Server
terms.outcomes: Setting up a simple web server on the Pi. Accessing a custom webpage from another device on the same network.

terms.title: Bluetooth Chat
terms.outcomes: Pairing devices and sending simple text strings between them over Bluetooth.

terms.title: IoT Controller
terms.outcomes: Controlling the LEDs/Motors from a smartphone browser over the local Wi-Fi network.

safety: Understanding public vs. private networks. The risks of open Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, 'Bluebugging', and the importance of encryption when sending data over the air.

title: Telecommunications: SIM & 4G/5G
summary: The final hardware component—the cellular modem—transforms the computer into a true mobile phone. Students learn how cellular networks function and write scripts to send SMS and make calls.

terms.title: The SIM Card
terms.outcomes: What is a Subscriber Identity Module? Connecting a 4G HAT and inserting a SIM.

terms.title: AT Commands
terms.outcomes: Communicating directly with the modem using standard AT commands. checking signal strength and network status.

terms.title: Sending SMS
terms.outcomes: Writing a script to send and receive text messages programmatically.

terms.title: Making a Call
terms.outcomes: Initiating a voice call through the Pi. Routing audio to the microphone and speaker.

safety: Metadata retention: Understanding that even if the content of a call is private, the 'who, when, and where' (metadata) is tracked by telecom operators. Spam calls and SMS phishing ('smishing').
